## Travel Medicines to Carry on Vacations and Road Trips

Stay healthy while on the road with travel medicines. These small packs fit easily in handbags and luggage, so you can take them just about anywhere.

## **Travel Medicine Essentials**

Fun as vacations are, they require lots of planning, especially if you'll be gone for several days or weeks. Your travel medicines shoud be part of this planning. While it's usually not too difficult to find medications for common ailments, such as [migraines](https://www.cvs.com/minuteclinic/services/migraine-headache) or hay fever, wherever your travels take you, it's always better to have what you need in advance. Some medicines you might want to bring with you while traveling include:

- [Pain relievers](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/pain-fever/pain-relievers)

- Allergy medicines

- Anti-diarrhea medicines

- Heartburn relievers


If you're taking any prescription medicines, ensure your supply will last your entire trip. Always keep these medicines in their original containers with the doctor's labeling intact, and bring your prescription and any necessary supporting documentation, such as a letter from your physician.

Different rules apply to domestic and international travel, and it's best to check what you can take with you in advance. If you're unsure, ask your doctor, pharmacist, airline customer service or the TSA.

## **Build Your Travel Medicine Kit**

Create a travel medicine kit to keep track of everything you need for health and well-being while on vacation. Start by thinking about the everyday conditions you may need to manage, such as heartburn or allergies. While some OTC medicines for these ailments are available in smaller packs, you can also typically transfer medicine into [travel-size storage containers](https://www.cvs.com/shop/beauty/beauty-tools-accessories/trial-travel-size-storage-containers) if you're not flying abroad.

Besides medicines, pack a few essential first-aid supplies, such as bandages and antiseptic ointment. Look for [travel-size personal care products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/trial-travel-size-personal-care) in case your favorite shampoo or moisturizer isn't available at your destination.

Cosmetics often come in smaller, easier-to-carry packages, but switching to [travel-size beauty products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/beauty/trial-travel-size-beauty) might be a better option. That way, you don't have to worry about losing expensive makeup or damaging it during transit.

## **Carry-On Medication Essentials**

Just because a certain product is available as a travel-size medicine doesn't mean bringing it on international flights or in your carry-on luggage is okay, as some OTC medications aren't legal everywhere. Always check the regulations that apply to your destination first.

When bringing allowed carry-on medications, consider getting a prescription, even for OTC medicines, to justify your use. Keep products in their original packaging to streamline the security check, and be mindful of liquid restrictions. However, the 100ml liquid limit generally doesn't apply to medically necessary items, provided you declare them.

## Health Products to Manage Everyday Conditions

Feel prepared for any situation with household health products. Our range of OTC medicines and wellness essentials helps you manage everyday conditions, such as colds, allergies, headaches and digestive problems, to keep your family comfortable.

## OTC Medicine for Everyday Relief

Even if you're extremely careful, you'll likely get the occasional cold or muscle ache. While these everyday conditions are easy to manage without any health products, OTC medicines, such as decongestants, may help ease symptoms and get you back to normal sooner.

Some household medicines are practically essentials, as having them on hand helps avoid disruptions to work, hobbies and social events. You don't need a whole cupboard full of products, but it's smart to keep [pain relievers](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/pain-fever/pain-relievers), cold and flu medicines and an antacid on hand. That way, when illnesses or injuries occur, you won't need to leave the house for medicine and can focus on rest and recovery instead.

## Health and Wellness Products

Good health and medicine go hand-in-hand. Whether you're trying to quit smoking or struggling to sleep, the right products can help make these challenges more manageable.

Every household can also benefit from having a [first aid kit](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/first-aid/first-aid-kits-accessories) that contains health essentials, such as bandages, antiseptics and sterile gauze. Add a few ointments for poison ivy, burns or insect bites, and you can handle most minor injuries.

However, not every condition is visible. For those that aren't, look to home test kits. These allow you to check your cholesterol or screen for common conditions, such as thyroid disease or food sensitivities, in the comfort of your own home. See your doctor for further tests to confirm the diagnosis.

## Health and Medicine Products for Summer

Allergy season is in full swing, and stocking up on the right health products is important to ensure you're well-prepared. Whether your main concern is seasonal allergies or you're experiencing poison ivy rashes, you can choose from plenty of health and medicine products.

For symptoms like sneezing and itchy eyes, [Claritin non-drowsy allergy relief liqui-gels](https://www.cvs.com/shop/claritin-24hr-non-drowsy-allergy-relief-liqui-gels-prodid-1011692) are formulated to provide up to 24 hours of relief for indoor and outdoor allergies. For summer rashes, consider adding a product like [Benadryl extra strength anti-itch gel](https://www.cvs.com/shop/benadryl-extra-strength-cooling-relief-anti-itch-gel-prodid-1012093) to your regime. This product provides cooling relief against most outdoor itches, from bug bites and poison ivy rashes to sunburns.

## Medicine to Help Tackle Summer Illnesses

While the return of warm days is welcome, summer is often a time when allergens and seasonal viruses spread. Make sure to stock up on medicines and health products designed to help you feel better while sickness runs its course. [Tylenol cold & flu multi-symptom liquid gels](https://www.cvs.com/shop/tylenol-cold-flu-multi-symptom-liquid-gels-12-ct-prodid-694103) provide quick relief from headaches, body aches, fever, sore throat and cough. For children, try [CVS children’s cold & cough relief liquid](https://www.cvs.com/shop/cvs-children-s-cold-cough-relief-liquid-grape-4-fl-oz-prodid-429542) to help quell stubborn cold and flu symptoms.

## Eye Care Essentials for Your Family

Protect, hydrate and soothe your eyes through every season with eye care essentials from CVS. Stock up on eye care essentials, from gels and drops to eye health supplements, contact lens solutions and eyeglass cleaners for your family's vision care needs.

## **Enhance Your Vision With Effective Eye Care Products**

View the world comfortably and easily with the help of high-quality eye products. Lock in moisture with eye drops made for dryness relief, or try gel drops or lubricants for red, irritated eyes. Blue light glasses and computer glasses help filter harmful rays, making screen time more comfortable. Gel eye masks may also provide relief after a busy day of work or gaming on your computer.

Wipe away smudges and streaks from your glasses with an eyeglass cleaning kit, or protect contacts with contact lens cleaners. When it's time to replace your contacts, you can buy contact lenses for your family from various popular brands.

## **Targeted Eye Treatments for Your Needs**

[Managing dry skin](https://www.cvs.com/learn/health/skin-health-conditions/how-to-manage-dry-skin) can be simple with the right products, and so can treating dry eyes. Explore therapeutic dry eye treatment options for your family, including:

- Eye gels

- Eye drops

- Artificial tears

- Eye masks


You may also want to consider computer glasses, such as lenses that block blue light, if computer use causes dry eyes. [Eye health supplements](https://www.cvs.com/shop/vitamins/supplements/lutein) might also help prevent discomfort and irritation, but check with your vision care provider first.

Enjoy quick relief from itchy, watery eyes with allergy treatments for your eyes, such as eye drops with antihistamines in them. Cooling eye masks and sprays can reduce fatigue, while eyelid wipes may refresh and rejuvenate your eyes. Find eye care products and treatments for every concern, whether you have dryness from screen time or need relief for itchy eyes.

## **Eye Relief for Discomfort**

It's important to avoid scratching your body when you have [itchy skin](https://www.cvs.com/learn/health/skin-health-conditions/relieve-itchy-skin), as scratching can make you feel worse. The same is often true for itchy eyes. Unless your doctor recommends otherwise, avoid rubbing your eyes when they itch, and try eye-relief products, such as gels or drops, instead.

Soothe dry, irritated eyes with refreshing lubricants, or use hydrating eye drops to conceal redness after an exhausting night. Cooling eye masks work to rejuvenate tired eyes, helping you look refreshed even when life gets hectic. Gentle [eye washes](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/eye-care/eye-wash-solutions) can remove debris and unwanted substances from your eyes, letting you see the world safely and clearly. When you stock up on [seasonal skin care](https://www.cvs.com/learn/beauty/skin-care/seasonal-skin-care) products, remember to grab seasonal eye care essentials as well, such as allergy relief drops.

## Explore Personal Care Products for Your Hair and Body

Show your body some love with personal care products that gently buff away rough patches and hydrate dry skin. Complete your beauty routine with essentials for hair care, feminine hygiene, odor control and other must-have products.

## Essential Personal Care Items

Elevate your bath and body routine with personal care products formulated with nourishing ingredients. Soothe skin with vitamin E, help conceal the signs of aging with skin-plumping collagen or soften irritated skin with hydrating shea butter. Stock up on toiletries and pamper yourself from head to toe, whether you need a new razor or another bottle of your go-to shampoo.

Find quality [hair removal products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/hair-removal-shave) that simplify your shaving routine and give you sleek legs, stubble-free underarms or a smooth upper lip. After stocking up on hair removal products and skin care essentials, explore a selection of feminine care products that encourage overall health and comfort for every stage of your cycle. Find products for feminine hygiene, period relief, menopause support and more at CVS.

## Personal Hygiene Products for Self-Care

Maintain a fresh, healthy smile with a selection of toothbrushes, toothpaste, floss, mouthwash and teeth whitening products. Find essential personal care items for your [oral care](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/oral-care) needs in a variety of styles and flavors, from electric toothbrushes in vibrant hues to breath-freshening mint mouthwash. After caring for your teeth, combat specific skin concerns with targeted skin care solutions. Find products for acne, dry skin, eczema and other challenges from your favorite brands when you shop online or at your local store.

Finish your signature look by creating the perfect hair care routine for your unique hair type. Shop for shampoos, conditioners and styling products for every type of hair, whether you have tight curls, loose waves or fine locks. Styling tools, such as curling irons and wands, can also help transform your tresses.

## Summer Personal Care Essentials

Choosing the right personal care products for summer is important. Warm weather usually mean spending more time outside. From [sunscreen](https://www.cvs.com/shop/beauty/skin-care/sun-tanning?icid=shop-beauty-skin-nav-sun-tanning) and [deodorant](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/deodorant-antiperspirant?icid=shop-pc-category-featured-deodorant) to everyday hygiene products and toiletries, CVS offers a wide selection to help you feel prepared for the season.

With more sun exposure, protecting your skin from harmful rays can help prevent painful sunburns and visible signs of aging. And as you spend more time out and about, taking care of your smile matters, too. CVS has you covered with toothbrushes, dental floss, teeth‑whitening kits, and mouthwash to keep your mouth fresh and your smile sparkling.

## Beat Summer Skin Irritation with Personal Care Must‑Haves

When summer hits, heat and humidity are in full swing — and for a lot of people, that means sweaty, irritated and uncomfortable skin. But don't let the summer heat get you down. Instead, get relief with products like [CeraVe Moisturizing Cream](https://www.cvs.com/shop/cerave-moisturizing-cream-body-and-face-moisturizer-16-oz-prodid-1130433). It provides long-lasting hydration and helps keep your skin barrier healthy, even when the sun and heat are working against you. For especially itchy or irritated skin, try a body lotion or wash specifically designed to calm and soothe. [Eucerin Eczema Relief Cream Body Wash](https://www.cvs.com/shop/eucerin-eczema-relief-cream-body-wash-13-5-oz-prodid-377723) helps ease dry, itchy skin so you can enjoy the season without the discomfort.

## HSA- and FSA-Eligible Products

Did you know you can buy many common drugstore items using a Flexible Spending Account or Health Savings Account? CVS Pharmacy stocks hundreds of HSA- and FSA-eligible items, including pain relievers, antihistamines, bandages and cold medicines.

FSAs and HSAs enable you to set aside pre-tax income for qualified medical expenses.

FSAs are provided by employers. You choose the amount to contribute from your paycheck. Some employers may also contribute funds. Typically, FSAs are subject to a “use it or lose it” rule and unused funds are lost at the end of the plan year.

HSAs are similar to FSAs, but you need an HSA-eligible high-deductible health plan to qualify. HSAs have higher contribution limits than FSAs. Funds carry over and remain in your account if you change jobs or retire.

Many people use these health benefits to pay for medical appointments and prescription medicines. You can also buy various over-the-counter products that support your health and wellness. Visit our frequently asked questions page to learn more about [how FSAs and HSAs work](https://www.cvs.com/shop/merch/FSA-HSA/FSA-HSA-resources?widgetID=nlvvdnle&mc=cvscontentpage).

Check with your plan administrator for a complete list of qualified medical expenses and any specific rules or restrictions.

## HSA- and FSA-Eligible Items

FSAs and HSAs enable you to personalize your health spending. You can decide which products to buy based on your needs. Items such as sunscreen, hand sanitizer, antacids and cough drops don't need a prescription to qualify. Some over the counter (OTC) products, like vitamins, are eligible with a doctor's letter. Check with your plan administrator for details about eligible items.

Plan ahead so you don't lose your FSA contributions. If your spending deadline is approaching, consider stocking up on items you need in the future. Below is a list of common FSA- and HSA-approved items.

### Health and Medicine

You can use FSA dollars to buy approved [health and medicine products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/q/true/fs) for common ailments. Keep [cough, cold and flu remedies](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/q/true/fs) in your medicine cabinet to manage symptoms once they start. [Pain relief products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/pain-fever/q/true/fs) can help ease discomfort from arthritis, migraines and fever. Some [allergy and asthma products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/allergy-sinus/q/true/fs) also qualify for FSAs.

### First Aid Supplies

FSA-covered items include [first aid supplies](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/first-aid/q/true/fs) for treating minor cuts, scrapes and injuries. Pick up a first-aid kit for your home, car or office, or create one based on your needs. [Bandages](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/first-aid/bandages-gauze-tape/q/true/fs), [antiseptics](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/first-aid/antibiotic-antiseptic/q/true/fs) and [itch and rash treatments](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/first-aid/itch-rash-treatment/q/true/fs) are useful for accidents and emergencies.

### Eye Care

Many people use an FSA or HSA to buy eligible over-the-counter [eye care products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/eye-care/q/true/fs). These include [nonprescription reading glasses](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/eye-care/reading-glasses) and eye drops for irritated, itchy or red eyes. You can also use your flexible spending account for contact lens supplies. Look for [cleaning and disinfection solutions](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/eye-care/contact-lens-solution/q/true/fs), rewetting drops and lens cases.

### Feminine Care and Family Planning

[Feminine care products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/feminine-care/q/true/fs), including pads, tampons and menstrual cups, are covered under an FSA or HSA. You can also buy over-the-counter (OTC) medicines to [help treat yeast infections](https://www.cvs.com/shop/personal-care/feminine-care/yeast-infection-treatments/q/true/fs) and [ease pain from urinary tract infections](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/pain-fever/urinary-tract-infection/q/true/fs). Explore [family planning products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/sexual-wellness/family-planning/q/true/fs), such as pregnancy, ovulation and fertility tests, to manage your reproductive health.

### Suncare

[FSA-eligible sunscreen products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/beauty/skin-care/sun-tanning/sunscreen/q/true/fs) can help protect your skin from sun damage. Generally, broad-spectrum sunscreens with an SPF of 15 or greater are FSA-eligible. [After-sun cooling sprays and gels](https://www.cvs.com/shop/content/sunburn-relief/q/true/fs) that relieve pain from sunburns are also covered.

### Baby and Child Care

Support your child's wellness with a range of [FSA-eligible purchases for babies and kids](https://www.cvs.com/shop/baby-kids/q/true/fs). Children's pain relievers and saline mists can make kids more comfortable when they're ill. Electrolyte solutions can help them stay hydrated as they recover. You can also apply your FSA balance to buy nighttime underpants for children who are potty training.

### Wellness Devices

Many [home health care products](https://www.cvs.com/shop/home-health-care/q/true/fs), such as bathroom safety equipment and walkers, help support safety at home. If you're healing from injuries, consider [FSA-eligible braces and supports](https://www.cvs.com/shop/home-health-care/braces-supports/q/true/fs), such as knee wraps and back stabilizers. Glucose monitoring systems and test strips help you stay on top of your health and are an important part of routine [diabetes care](https://www.cvs.com/shop/home-health-care/diabetes-care/q/true/fs).

## FAQs

## Can I Use My FSA/HSA Card Online?

Yes, HSA- and FSA-eligible items are clearly marked on the CVS Pharmacy® website. When you check out, enter your FSA/HSA card number as a form of payment. You can add other payment options to pay for the purchase balance. Flex spending eligible items are also listed in your email confirmation and online order history.

## Can I Get Reimbursed if I Pay Out of Pocket?

Most plans reimburse you if you pay out of pocket for FSA-eligible products. Keep your receipt and ask your plan administrator for details.

## Are Shipping and Tax Covered?

Often, the sales tax and shipping fees for the purchase of FSA- and HSA-qualified items are covered. Your HR representative or plan administrator can provide more information.

_**\*Health savings account (HSA) and flexible spending account (FSA) eligible items may vary by benefits administrator and with changes in Internal Revenue Service (IRS) rules. Check with your benefits administrator.**_

## Cold Medicine
Over-the-counter cold medicine can help alleviate uncomfortable symptoms associated with illness. Whether you need to get through the day or you want to be able to rest more comfortably, find a wide selection of cold and flu medicine at CVS.

## **Conquer Symptoms With Cold and Flu Medicine**
[Cold medicine](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/cold-flu-medicine/q/Top_Rated/tp) lets you target specific symptoms associated with the common cold, such as nasal congestion, cough and sore throat.

CVS cold medicine options offer relief for many cold and [flu symptoms](https://www.cvs.com/learn/health/cough-cold-flu/flu-medicines-tips), including chest congestion and cough.

[Cold and flu medicine for babies and kids](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/cough-cold-flu-for-children) is also available. Chest rub made with ingredients such as eucalyptus, lavender and chamomile may help alleviate chest congestion symptoms, and cough syrup for daytime and nighttime is available from familiar brands, such as [Tylenol](https://www.cvs.com/shop/brand-shop/t/tylenol) and Zarbee's.

## **Cold and Cough Medicine Solutions**
Some cold and cough medicines contain ingredients to help relieve nasal congestion and sinus pressure. [Nasal sprays](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/sinus-relief) are a great choice for treating nasal passages as they contain ingredients to relieve sinus pressure and congestion.

These medicines contain sleep aids in addition to cold/flu-fighting ingredients. Some are specifically for nighttime coughs, and others, such as NyQuil, are for general cold/flu relief at night. Combine a nighttime cold/flu or cough formula with a humidifier, chest rub or other [homeopathic remedies](https://www.cvs.com/shop/merch/homeopathic-remedies) for a more comfortable sleeping environment.

## **Cold and Flu Medicine Essentials**
Liquids, tablets and chewables are all available to suit your specific needs. Pain-relief ingredients in these cold and flu medicines can help alleviate body aches and pains.

**Explore Cough, Cold, Flu**

## Sore Throat Relief

In most cases, a sore throat is caused by an infection from a virus, such as a cold or the flu. Allergies are another common cause. For some patients, sore throats will get better on their own, but not for all. Therefore, if you are at all concerned, it’s always best to see your doctor. In cases where your sore throat is caused by a bacterial infection, you may need antibiotics from your doctor. But if it turns out that you just need to wait out your sore throat, how do you cope while you’re waiting for your symptoms to reduce? You don’t have to just put up with that scratching, raw sensation or the pain that often goes with it! There are a number of ways that you can help reduce the discomfort of a sore throat like [sore throat drops](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/cough-medicine/sore-throat-relief/q/Drops/fm). If you're still experiencing cold or flu symptoms, taking a [flu pain reliever](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/cold-flu-medicine/q/Pain_Relief/cn) may also provide relief.

## How to soothe a sore throat

- **Lozenges.** Sucking on throat lozenges can provide temporary relief from sore throat pain. [Throat lozenges](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/cough-cold-flu/cough-medicine/cough-drops) formulated with menthol can be especially helpful, as the ingredient can gently numb your throat to help temporarily decrease unpleasant sensations of burning, scratchiness, and pain. Do not give lozenges to young children or anyone who has difficulty swallowing, as they are a choking hazard.

- **Throat spray.** [Throat sprays](https://www.cvs.com/shop/chloraseptic-max-sore-throat-spray-wild-berries-prodid-465124) contain mild numbing agents such as menthol, which may temporarily decrease the pain associated with a sore throat. Herbal sprays formulated with echinacea and sage are options as well, although scientific evidence of their effectiveness is limited.

- **Salt water.** Gargling with warm water mixed with salt a few times a day may help bring down swelling and temporarily ease your throat pain. The recommended dissolution is 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of salt in 1 cup of warm water.

- **Warm tea**. Drinking warm (not hot!) tea, especially with honey or lemon in it, may help ease your sore throat symptoms and bring you some temporary relief. If you don’t like tea, try warm water with honey or sip some warm broth. Be sure to drink plenty of fluids throughout the day to help prevent dehydration, which can worsen sore throat pain. And be sure to note – never give honey to a child under 1 year old.

- **Use a humidifier**. A [cool air humidifier](https://www.cvs.com/shop/cvs-health-compact-fill-humidifier-prodid-948171) can help get rid of dry air that can further irritate a sore throat. If you choose to use a humidifier, be sure to clean it regularly to help avoid disseminating mold or bacteria into the room.

- **Use steam**. Stand or sit in a steamy bathroom for several minutes if you are able. The humidity in the air can help soothe throat pain and may make breathing feel easier.

- **Try over the counter pain relief medicine**. An over the counter pain reliever such as [ibuprofen](https://www.cvs.com/shop/health-medicine/pain-fever/pain-relievers/q/Ibuprofen/ki) may help reduce inflammation and take the edge off your sore throat pain. Be sure to follow the directions on the label carefully, and check with your doctor or pharmacist before taking any over the counter pain relievers.

- **Raise your head up**. If you’re suffering from nasal congestion along with a sore throat, consider propping your head up with an extra pillow. This may help you breathe through your nose more easily and reduce the amount that you have to breathe with your mouth open, which can dry out your throat and may exacerbate throat pain.

- **Try a decongestant**. Nasal congestion can result in mucus draining from your sinuses down your throat, which can worsen sore throat pain. A [decongestant](https://www.cvs.com/shop/sudafed-pe-sinus-congestion-max-strength-non-drowsy-tablets-36ct-prodid-1011649) or [antihistamine](https://www.cvs.com/shop/content/antihistamines) can help control your nasal congestion so that you can feel more comfortable. Be sure to follow the directions on the label carefully, and check with your doctor or pharmacist before taking any over the counter decongestants or antihistamines.


Often, when you have a sore throat, one of your top priorities is to get relief! The good news is that CVS can help. CVS offers a variety of products that may help with sore throat relief, and some of the recommendations above may provide you with some temporary relief. But if you have questions or concerns about your sore throat, you should contact your doctor, especially if your sore throat pain persists, is very severe, or concerns you. He or she can run tests to help determine the cause of your sore throat and make appropriate treatment recommendations. Remember – CVS is here to help with sore throat relief!
